x: Coming home, however, Canard was the first of our boys, Coleman having had the misfortune to cast a shoe and so to fall back several places.
I arrived at Clapham Junction expecting to find a crowd, but found only Mitchell and Canard had turned up. After waiting for some time we decided to carry-on and hope for the best.

G Tyrer, a veteran, who was second last year in the corresponding race, was limit man, and went off at his usual jog-trot. He was overhauled, however, after covering about a mile, Canard passing him in company with Colman and Strange S.

Canard and Dewberry both had off days, the latter's old fault of dashing off at the start again led to his own undoing and until he curbs his impetuosity and runs more evenly he will find it difficult to last out a race.
Canard, Chorley, Fletcher, and a newcomer in Carter, all ran prominently and should still further improve on their positions in future races.

Runners passed by until Fletcher came along, 30th, and Canard, 37th; Chorley and Coleman were still further behind, and as Mitcham and Reading's fourth man had already passed it did not look any too rosy for the Bels.
Our runners did very well in finishing second in the team race, and Michael and Canard distinguished themselves by finishing in the first half-dozen.
Michael ran very well to finish 6th, while Canard made a welcome re-appearance and was second man home for us. Martin was just behind him, and then came Goldsworthy to complete our scoring four.
An old member of ours, Canard, ran for the R.A.F. and finished 25th. Crewdson, a former member of Croydon Harriers, also with the airmen, filled 21 position.
